newsitem.title: USA: Hilton CEO sees Ladbroke ties as priority.
newsitem.headline: Hilton CEO sees Ladbroke ties as priority.

text.p: After a busy 1996, Hilton Hotels Corp Chief Executive Officer Stephen Bollenbach will first look to strengthen his overseas ties with Ladbroke Group Plc, then resume the acquisition track in 1997.

"The most important thing next year is to really complete and do as much as possible with Ladbroke. Re-uniting Hilton is really the big value creator for us," Bollenbach said in an interview on Thursday. "It won't be as (glitzy) as an acquisition like Bally (Entertainment Inc), but it will be every bit as important to our shareholders."

In August, Hilton and Ladbroke, owner of Hilton International Inc, unveiled an alliance in which they will work together on sales, marketing and promotional programs and seek out opportunities for hotel development.
Hilton also said it would acquire $180 million of equity in Ladbroke, which amounted to a five percent stake.

The deal led to some market players to speculate that Hilton would move to acquire all of Hilton International, but Bollenbach said he believes Hilton can get as much value out of the current arrangement as an outright accquisition.
Still, acquisitions in the gambling arena will be on Hilton's menu, as many market players expect. Though any new deal would likely be later rather than sooner.
"The people who should be sellers have stars in their eyes as to what their values are," Bollenbach said. "Once they are realistic on prices, we intend to be acquirors."
He gave no timetable for snapping up a new company, but said Hilton is ready to move when prices come down.
Mid-size gambling companies are on Hilton's plate because of the cost savings a huge company like Hilton could bring to the table, especially where the cost of debt is concerned.
"You take mid-level companies that finance construction at junk bond rates, and we can finance it at six percent," he said. "That's the kind of target that makes sense for us."
Harrah's Entertainment Inc is one acquisition target that is most speculated about in financial markets, but Bollenbach did not name specific companies.

On the subject of cutting interest costs, however, Bollenbach said Hilton would look to the bond markets toward the first of 1997 to help refinance debt from its $3.0 billion acquisition of Bally. He said the company would most likely issue debt with maturities in the seven to 10-year range.

It has been widely reported that Hilton expects to save as much as $60 million in annual costs after the Bally merger, nearly half of that through reduced interest expense. Bollenbach called the $60 million figure, "a conservative number."
